messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident S2 triggered: anomalous GPU memory growth in kv-cache hosts (asia-west-1). Alerts: repeated cudaMalloc failures and fragmentation spikes. Pager sent to #incidents and @sre-oncall. Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/kv-cache-frag

alex.prasad: I'm on it. seeing same on rollups-5 and rollups-7. top of dmesg shows repeated cuda allocation failures ~30s apart.

maria: noticed a correlation with last night's continuous-batching rollout (max_batch_tokens from 512 -> 2048). heaps of small KV entries flagged.

sre-oncall: quick ask — can we throttle batching to reduce simultaneous KV cache allocation pressure? If yes, let's do that first.

eng-runtime-lead: Agreed. Patch ready to pin continuous batching to previous behavior. Suggest immediate hotfix: set max_batch_tokens=512 and disable dynamic_batch_expansion. Will push to canary then all.

samir: Pushing config to canary now (rollups-1). Command: ```curl -X POST https://infra-api/local/config -d '{"service":"kv-cache","max_batch_tokens":512,"dynamic_batch_expansion":false}'```

ops-bot: deploy started for rollups-1. CI checks passed. Estimated 2m to complete.

alex.prasad: Meanwhile I'm running a diagnostic to measure allocator fragmentation. Grepping ptx logs: ```grep -E "cudaMalloc|fragment" /var/log/kvcache/*.log | tail -n 50``` shows many small allocations around 4-8MB failing after fragmentation threshold.

maria: We should also trigger an immediate KV cache GC for large prefixes and drop stale prefix caches. Command (dry-run): ```/opt/kvcache/bin/kvgc --evict-old --threshold 0.75```

customer-ops: Heads up — we have 2 active customers (acct-id: AC-342, AC-119) on dedicated pools in asia-west; they may see elevated latency or 502s while we mitigate. I'm preparing comms.

eng-runtime-lead: Canary complete, pushing to all rollups. ops-bot: continue.

ops-bot: deploy completed for rollups-2..8. Rollout status: success.

sre-oncall: After config rollback, immediate error rate on kv-cache hosts dropped by ~60% and OOM alerts ceased for canary cluster. Monitoring for 10m.

samir: Triggered KVGC evictions on affected hosts. Observed reclaimed ~6GB on rollups-7 and ~4.2GB on rollups-5.

alex.prasad: Still seeing elevated fragmentation metric (arena_fragment_ratio ~0.48). PyTorch allocator is not consolidating freed blocks quickly. Recommending temporary environment tweak: set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64,garbage_collection_threshold:0.2 (example).

maria: If we change TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF we need service restart for the runtime process. Can we do rolling restarts?

eng-runtime-lead: We'll avoid mass restarts. Plan: pick two least-loaded pools, restart runtime there with updated env var, observe for 15m, then continue. samir, coordinate restarts.

samir: Restarting rollups-5 runtime (step 1). Command: ```systemctl restart redwood-kv-runtime && journalctl -u redwood-kv-runtime -n 200 -f```

ops-bot: restart acknowledged on rollups-5.

samir: rollups-5 back up. Post-restart fragmentation down to 0.22 on that host, reclaimed ~8GB. Latency p50 improved ~18%.

customer-ops: Both impacted accounts report reduced error rates. No formal incident ticket created by customers yet, but support queue saw 3 incoming messages.

alex.prasad: Good. Continue controlled restarts across other affected nodes (rollups-7 next). We should also schedule a kernel-level arena tuning: increase min_split_size and reduce max_cached_bytes in the allocator shim. I'll open a follow-up RFC.

maria: For immediate safety, let's keep continuous batching disabled for 24h and set a guard: new rollouts must not increase max_batch_tokens beyond 512 without perf sign-off. Documented in the rollout checklist.

sre-oncall: Noting timeline for handoff: I'll stay for 60m then hand to @maria for overnight. Please post final status before I sign off.

eng-runtime-lead: I'll coordinate a postmortem today morning with traces attached. Root hypotheses: 1) continuous batching increase created allocation bursts; 2) PyTorch/CUDA malloc fragmentation exacerbated by many mid-sized KV allocations; 3) allocator tunables and GC cadence insufficient under new workload.

ops-bot: Incident: mitigation in place. Severity reduced to S3. Next actions: telemetry retention snapshots, heapdumps for two affected hosts, RFC for allocator tuning.

customer-ops: Drafted customer note for AC-342/AC-119: "We've applied mitigations to reduce memory pressure and restored stability; monitoring continues. No data loss expected." Will send when ops-bot marks incident stable.

alex.prasad: Quick checklist to capture: ```- revert continuous batch expansion
- run KVGC on affected pools
- rolling restart with TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF tweak
- open RFC for allocator arena tuning
- postmortem with timelines + customer impact```

maria: I'm taking handoff. leaving a H: (kidding). I'll update the incident doc and schedule the postmortem. @sre-oncall you can sign off.

sre-oncall: Signing off for now. If anything regresses, re-pager. Great job everyone. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident thread closed for on-call shift at 1773457025.
